citation.title: Temporal variability in summertime bottom hypoxia in shallow areas of Mobile Bay, Alabama

mooring.adcp: RDI Workhorse Sentinel 600 kHz; bottom mounted; 20-min current profiles; 0.1-m vertical bins

published_relationships.salinity_gradient_definition: upper minus bottom salinity over approximately 2.5 m vertical separation
published_relationships.low_gradient_result: When salinity gradient was <2 psu, about 1% of observations were hypoxic and mean bottom DO was nearly 6 mg/L.
published_relationships.strong_gradient_result: When salinity gradient remained >4 psu, approximately 65-78% of observations were hypoxic and mean bottom DO remained below 2 mg/L; hypoxia occurred almost all the time when gradient exceeded 8 psu absent extreme events.
published_relationships.dynamic_result: Bottom DO increased during destratification events and decreased rapidly after stratification re-established; the paper concludes oxygen supply can be exhausted within hours to days after mixing terminates.

model_relevance: This is a high-value independent vertical-mooring dataset for Stage-1 hypoxic-water loading because it has known sensor heights, bottom DO concentration, upper/bottom salinity and 20-minute cadence. The published threshold behavior independently supports salinity-gradient nonlinearity and rapid reload after destratification. Raw time-series bytes have not yet been located in a public archive, so the record remains a source lead and no row-level feature/backtest is claimed.
next_action: Recover the original 2004 time-series from DISL/USA/NOAA or another public archive using the exact coordinates, dates, instrument names and publication provenance; then hash, normalize and independently reproduce the paper's gradient-hypoxia relationships before use in any shadow model.
guardrails: Published aggregate relationships are not substitute raw observations.
No event/non-event labels are inferred from the 2004 mooring period.
Do not count this source as ingested until raw rows are recovered, hashed and normalized.
No production feature or weight change.
